newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Cocoa price rise technical say traders.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa price rise technical say traders.

text.p: Cocoa fundamentals have not changed in the past weeks, physical supplies from West Africa remain plentiful in Europe and the market is looking to an Ivorian crop above one million tonnes, traders said.
"The rise (in futures prices) has been mostly technical," one Continental Europe physical trader said. "There is a lot of cocoa around and the fundamentals don't really justify it."
The active May contract in London peaked at 945 stg on Wednesday, sharply up on a week ago when it was down at 880.
A large crop from the world's biggest grower should put the deficit this season around 100,000 tonnnes, traders here said.

This commonly held view differs sharply from that held by commodity brokers GNI, which this week said it was sticking to its forecast of a 180,000 tonne deficit. It added that a 50,000 tonne swing either way was possible in the Ivorian crop but that problems with with the Ivorian mid-crop were unlikely.
There is still some concern that dry weather there during February may hurt the crop, expected to be near 150,000 tonnes.
"It's a little too early to say if the drought there will have any effect but it's something the market is watching," one industry source said.
Analysts have said they would be looking for a considerable increase in rainfall this month to prevent downward revisions of the mid-crop size.
Physical prices have kept pace with moves on the terminal market and differentials have remained steady. Traders noted Ivorian cocoa for April trading around 30 stg under May.
Other origins were absent from the physical market.
